This project establishes a new Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU) Site hosted by the Department of Computer Science at UNC Greensboro. Ten students will receive research training each summer in the foundations of graph machine learning and network analysis and their concrete applications in real-life networks. Graphs and networks have become ubiquitous in various scientific disciplines ranging from the Internet of Things, online social networks, brain networks, and molecules to protein-protein interaction networks. Analysis of large-scale networks can bring significant advances to our understanding of complex systems. Existing methods are purely empirical or lack in-depth foundational exploration, thus limited in processing complex graph and network data. This project aims to provide students the opportunity to undertake cutting-edge research in graphs and networks at a major research institute. The research training on Graph Learning and Network Analysis (GraLNA ) will contribute to developing a competitive next-generation network and AI workforce. Through various activities such as orientation workshops, invited lectures, hands-on projects, presentations, demos, and other professional development opportunities, undergraduate students will also enhance their professional skills.
The first objective of this GraLNA project is to provide an experience of doing solid research for a diverse group of students especially those from Primarily Undergraduate Institutions. Students will gain an increased proficiency in research skills as well as oral and written communication skills. The second objective is to advance the theoretical understanding of graph learning and optimization, and to also develop new approaches to handling diverse types of complexities in graph and network data. Notable types of complexities include the distributed nature of many real-world graph data, privacy concerns arising from sensitive relationships and interactions encoded in graphs and networks, and specialized network data that involves rich domain knowledge and regulatory constraints. Student participants will engage with research projects centered around distributed graph analysis, federated learning, optimization, private graph analysis, network security, and structural and functional brain network analysis. The third objective of this project is to provide for both student participants and faculty mentors professional training and growth through a series of professional development activities and also provide junior faculty and Ph.D. students mentoring and co-advising experience respectively.

This position is part of DFAS's Pathways Program, for current students/individuals accepted for enrollment in a qualifying educational program in an accredited institution, full or half-time basis. Applicants who indicate they meet the minimum qualifications will receive an email from assessments@USAHire.opm.gov to complete online assessments. Check your "Spam"/"Junk" folders. See below for more information!

You MUST submit proof of acceptance along with your current transcripts for consideration. If selected, must sign a Pathways Participant Agreement; provide course registration information at the start of each school term; and provide verification of academic status (official transcript) at the end of each academic term. The following are preferred degree categories: Accounting Business Administration with Accounting Concentration Masters of Business Administration with Accounting Concentration Masters of Accountancy The degree does not have to be related to the position/series; however to be eligible, candidate must meet the agency-developed or OPM qualification standards for the position to which the Intern may be converted. If you are relying on your education to meet qualification requirements: You MUST submit a copy of your transcript if you want to substitute your education for experience. If you claim qualifications based on education, and do not submit a transcript, your education will not be used in making a qualification determination and you may be found "not qualified". Two years of successfully completed education (by the end of the Spring 2027 term) above the high school level in any field for which high school graduation, or the equivalent, is a prerequisite may be substituted to meet the general experience required. NOTE: If you are relying on your education to meet qualification requirements: You MUST submit a copy of your transcript if you want to substitute your education for experience. If you claim qualifications based on education, and do not submit a transcript, your education will not be used in making a qualification determination and you may be found "not qualified". OR B. One year of generalized experience which demonstrates the ability to perform the duties of the position, is required. Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills, and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. PROGRAM COMPLETION AND CONVERSION ELIGIBILITY: Upon successful completion of their academic program and the internship program, interns may be converted to a term or permanent position in the competitive service consistent with agency needs, academic achievement, and demonstrated potential. The HBM Platform Architecture team defines the electrical, thermal, and power-delivery architectures that enable Micron's next-generation High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) solutions. Working closely with architecture, design, packaging, and technology teams, the organization drives innovation in signaling, power integrity, thermal management, and system optimization to support AI, high-performance computing, and data center applications.
As an HBM Platform Architecture Intern, you will contribute to the development of future HBM platforms by evaluating electrical, thermal, and power delivery architectures for advanced memory systems. You will work alongside experienced architects to analyze design trade-offs, develop modeling tools, and investigate solutions that improve performance, power efficiency, reliability, and scalability for next-generation memory products.

Perform signaling and timing analysis for on-die and off-die interfaces across multiple system and packaging topologies.
Develop and evaluate thermal models to analyze heat transfer, thermal performance, and design trade-offs in advanced memory systems.
Analyze power delivery networks (PDNs), including IR-drop, electromigration (EM), power integrity, and power grid optimization for advanced HBM architectures.
Develop modeling, simulation, and automation tools to support power delivery, thermal analysis, and architecture evaluation activities.
Collaborate with architecture, design, packaging, and technology teams to evaluate system-level trade-offs and support future HBM technology development.

0-2 years of relevant experience through internships, research projects, coursework, or academic projects in electrical engineering, VLSI design, signal integrity, power integrity, thermal analysis, semiconductor design, or related technical fields.

Coursework or project experience in analog design, I/O design, signaling, DRAM technologies, high-speed interfaces, packaging, or 2.5D/3D integration technologies.
Understanding of electrical systems, signal integrity, power delivery, circuit analysis, or semiconductor design fundamentals.
Ability to read and interpret technical specifications, datasheets, interface standards, and hardware documentation.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical communication skills.
Experience using AI-enabled tools and large language models (LLMs) such as Copilot, Claude, ChatGPT, or similar technologies as part of engineering workflows, with the ability to validate and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs.

Knowledge of semiconductor packaging, assembly processes, heterogeneous integration, or advanced packaging technologies.
Experience with analog design, I/O design, timing analysis, signal integrity, or system-level electrical modeling through coursework, research, or project work.
Experience with thermal modeling, computational analysis, power delivery analysis, IR-drop, electromigration (EM), or power integrity evaluations.
Knowledge of HBM, DRAM, memory interfaces, advanced interconnects, or high-speed signaling technologies.

Our Summer Internship Program:
Our Summer Internship Program (PLOT) offers an opportunity to gain meaningful experience in Marketing while building the foundation for a successful career. During this 12-week program, you'll learn from industry professionals, tackle real-world projects, and develop working knowledge of brand strategy, customer engagement, marketing communications, and campaign execution that support business growth across the agricultural industry. You'll have the opportunity to present your internship learnings directly to leadership. This is more than just an internship. It's your chance to make a real impact, build professional knowledge, and sharpen your abilities in a dynamic, results-driven environment. Successful completion of the PLOT program can also earn you a scholarship between $1,000 and $3,000.
Role Overview:
As a Wilbur-Ellis Marketing Intern, you'll gain experience in marketing strategy, content development, campaign execution, and market research. You'll work closely with the Marketing team to support initiatives that strengthen brand awareness, enhance customer engagement, and drive business growth.
Responsibilities may include assisting with digital and traditional marketing campaigns, creating and editing marketing content, supporting event planning and trade shows, analyzing campaign performance metrics, conducting market and customer research, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to develop promotional materials and customer-facing communications.
You'll have the opportunity to share your ideas, contribute creative solutions, and provide a unique perspective while supporting meaningful projects across the organization. At the conclusion of your internship, you'll prepare and present a final PowerPoint presentation highlighting your project work, key learnings, and overall experience.
What You Bring to the Role:
As an intern, we understand you may not already have extensive professional experience. We are seeking a college student pursuing a degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, Agriculture, Agricultural Business, Public Relations, Digital Media, Journalism, Graphic Design, or a related field with an interest in marketing and the agricultural industry.
Overall, we are looking for someone with strong written, verbal, and presentation skills; creativity and attention to detail; the ability to manage multiple priorities effectively; intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn; a self-starter who is eager to contribute ideas and collaborate across teams; and someone who brings their full self to work each day. We want to help you grow, and we want to learn from you, too.
Examples of What You May Gain:
Exposure to marketing strategy and brand management within a leading agribusiness organization
Experience developing marketing content and supporting integrated marketing campaigns
Opportunities to collaborate with marketing, sales, product, and business leadership teams
Development of communication, project management, research, and analytical skills
Hands-on experience with campaign planning, execution, and performance measurement
Exposure to customer insights, market trends, and industry best practices
Mentorship from experienced marketing professionals and business leaders
A deeper understanding of how marketing supports customer engagement, business growth, and brand success in the agricultural industry

In compliance with all states and cities requiring transparency of pay, the base compensation for this position ranges from $17.00 to $24.00 per hour. Note that wages may vary based on location, skills, and experience.
